dish: Kyoto chūka soba in a jet-black soy broth, with yakimeshi (dark fried rice)
n: Shinpuku Saikan Honten (新福菜館 本店)
address: 569 Higashi-Shiokōji Mukaihata-chō, Shimogyō-ku, Kyoto (5 min walk from JR Kyoto Station)
w: The black-soup original of Kyoto ramen: a yatai from 1938, at this spot by Kyoto Station since 1944 — the dark broth tastes far lighter than it looks.

dish: Creamy pork-and-chicken 'cloudy' tonkotsu-shōyu chūka soba; limited suji ramen
n: Chūka Soba Takayasu (中華そば 高安)
w: The originator of the cloudy, creamy-but-not-greasy broth that defines the Ichijōji ramen battleground; soup simmered 22+ hours.

dish: Coffee and the famous custard pudding in a 1934 ocean-liner-style salon
n: François Kissashitsu (フランソア喫茶室)
address: Nishikiyamachi-dōri by the Takase-gawa, Shimogyō-ku, Kyoto (1 min from Kyoto-Kawaramachi Stn)
w: Kyoto's iconic 1934 meikyoku-kissa; in 2003 the first café in Japan registered as a national Tangible Cultural Property.

dish: Home-roasted coffee (basement) and coffee with homemade doughnuts (ground floor)
w: Family-run since 1950 at Sanjō-Kawaramachi — two floors, two coffees; a cornerstone of Kyoto's kissaten culture.

dish: House-roasted specialty espresso and pour-over
w: Kyoto's third-wave pioneer, roasting its own beans since 2016, hidden in a machiya alley.

dish: Single-origin hand-drip coffee from a Kyoto-born roaster
address: Near JR Kyoto Station, Shimogyō-ku, Kyoto
w: Kyoto-born specialty brand that went global; a stand-up hand-drip bar a short walk from Kyoto Station.

dish: Espresso drinks and Kyoto latte, near Yasaka Pagoda
address: Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto (near Yasaka Pagoda and Kiyomizu-dera)
w: The minimalist % Arabica brand was born in Kyoto (2014); the Higashiyama shop is its flagship.

dish: Kuzukiri (arrowroot noodles) in black-sugar syrup, warabi-mochi, seasonal wagashi
address: Shijō-dōri, Gion, Higashiyama-ku, Kyoto (near Yasaka Shrine)
w: A Gion institution since the early 18th century; its tea room is the classic place for kuzukiri.

dish: Aburi-mochi — charcoal-grilled skewered mochi in white-miso sauce
address: Imamiya Shrine east approach, Murasakino, Kita-ku, Kyoto
w: The 'Honke' aburi-mochi house (c.1600), facing Ichiwa across Imamiya Shrine's approach.

dish: Aburi-mochi with white-miso sauce, a recipe kept since the year 1000
n: Ichiwa (一和 / 一文字屋和輔)
address: Imamiya Shrine east approach, Murasakino, Kita-ku, Kyoto
w: Said to be founded in 1000 (Chōhō 2) — among Japan's oldest confectioners; aburi-mochi at Imamiya Shrine's gate.

dish: Kizakura's Fushimi sake and Kizakura craft beer brewed on site, with izakaya plates
n: Kizakura Kappa Country (黄桜 カッパカントリー)
w: Brewery restaurant of Kizakura, one of Fushimi's big houses — the one place to drink both its sake and its own craft beer.

dish: Fushimi sake tasting sets (several breweries) in Gekkeikan's former head office
address: Former Gekkeikan headquarters, Fushimi Sake District, Fushimi-ku, Kyoto
w: The district's visitor café: sample sets from several Fushimi breweries in the old Gekkeikan HQ building.

dish: Yudofu (tofu simmered in kombu broth) and fresh yuba courses
address: In front of Nanzen-ji's Sanmon gate, Sakyō-ku, Kyoto
w: The classic Nanzen-ji yudofu house, set in an Edo-period medical-school building and garden by the temple gate.

dish: Yudofu set with dengaku and goma-dofu, in the garden of Chōshō-in
address: Beside Nanzen-ji, Sakyō-ku, Kyoto (garden of Chōshō-in)
w: Has served Zen-temple tofu for centuries in a garden just outside Nanzen-ji — the most atmospheric yudofu in town.

dish: Yudofu course in a light broth, with indoor and garden seating
n: Yudōfu Sagano (湯豆腐 嵯峨野)
w: Arashiyama's spacious, reliable yudofu house — the easy sit-down after the bamboo grove.

dish: Shōyu ramen in a 100% seafood dashi (no pork or chicken), stone-ground whole-wheat noodles
w: A 10-seat downtown counter whose 100% seafood broth is the anti-kotteri Kyoto bowl; Leaf KYOTO reports nine straight years of Michelin Bib Gourmand.

dish: Yakitori omakase — 'yakitori no saki', the future of yakitori
w: One MICHELIN Star yakitori counter; the name means 'the future of yakitori'.

dish: Tempura course — each ingredient shown before frying (vegetables and seafood from named producers)
address: B1F The Ritz-Carlton Kyoto, Nakagyō-ku, Kyoto
w: One MICHELIN Star tempura counter by the Kamo River, in the Ritz-Carlton.

dish: Charcoal yakitori course
w: MICHELIN-selected yakitori counter downtown.

dish: Sake by the glass — unfiltered, aged, fruity to dry — chosen by Israeli sake expert Yoram
w: A tiny, cult sake bar (a soba shop by day) whose owner's by-the-glass list is a crash course in nihonshu.

dish: ~1,200 sakes and ~600 single malts, tasting flights
w: Kyoto's 'temple to quality drinks' — a vast sake and malt-whisky library behind a polished counter.

dish: Classic cocktails and whisky in a former geisha house
w: Nordic-cool cocktail bar inside a converted Gion okiya.

dish: Theatrical 'elixir' cocktails by magician-bartender Christophe Rossi
w: A magician's cocktail den — floating couch, smoking elixirs — profiled by The Japan Times.

dish: Bespoke cocktails built around your tastes
w: Asia's 50 Best Bars (No. 81, 2023 51–100 list): a wood-panelled backstreet bar of under 30 seats.

dish: Bite-size, garlicky pan-fried gyoza with beer
n: Gyoza Hohei (ぎょうざ 歩兵)
w: Gion's beloved gyoza counter (a past Bib Gourmand, 2017 on) — Kyoto's answer to the after-hours dumpling.

dish: Kansai-style unagi grilled without steaming — unadon and hitsumabushi
address: Shijō Sakai-machi, Nakagyō-ku, Kyoto (steps from Nishiki Market)
w: The downtown eel specialist by Nishiki: crisp-skinned Kansai-style grilled unagi.

dish: Stand-up house-made soba in Kyoto udon-dashi, ten styles
w: A signboardless tachi-gui soba bar on Kiyamachi; soba from its own upstairs noodle workshop, open till 23:00.

dish: Hand-formed wagyu hambāgu steak with Awaji onion — classic yōshoku
n: Grill Hasegawa (グリル はせがわ)
address: 68 Oyama (Koyama) Shimo-Uchigawara-chō, Kita-ku, Kyoto (5 min from Kitaōji Stn)
w: Kitaōji's long-queued yōshoku institution — the definitive Kyoto hamburg steak.

dish: Dashimaki tamago — dashi-rich rolled omelette made to order
w: Nishiki's dashimaki specialist: watch the omelettes being rolled in copper pans.

dish: Charcoal-grilled fish and tai-kushi (sea-bream skewers); seafood tempura
w: A Nishiki fishmonger-grill since 1919 — grilled-fish skewers to eat walking the arcade.

dish: Tako-tamago — baby octopus skewered with a quail egg inside
w: Home of Nishiki's most photographed snack, the candied baby octopus with a quail-egg head.

dish: Hot soy-milk doughnuts and yuba croquettes from a tofu maker
w: The Kyoto-tofu maker's Nishiki stand — the soy-milk mini-doughnut queue is a market ritual.

dish: Uji matcha parfait and matcha soba
n: Itohkyuemon Uji Honten (伊藤久右衛門 宇治本店)
w: Uji tea house founded in 1832; its main-store café is a matcha-parfait pilgrimage.

dish: Matcha Mont Blanc, matcha parfait and matcha espresso
address: Uji, Kyoto (main store, in a 100-year-old building)
w: Tea merchant since 1860 whose Uji main store serves matcha desserts in a century-old building.

dish: Yomogi-mochi — mugwort mochi with red-bean paste, pounded at high speed in front of you
w: Nara's famous high-speed mochitsuki show; the mugwort mochi is eaten warm off the board.

dish: Kamameshi — rice cooked to order in an iron pot, topped with chicken, oyster, eel or crab
n: Shizuka Nara Park (志津香 公園店)
w: Nara's best-known kamameshi house; long lunchtime queues by Nara Park.

dish: Stone-ground handmade soba with a Togetsukyō river view
address: Beside Togetsukyō Bridge, Saga, Ukyō-ku, Kyoto
w: Soba in an old mansion overlooking the Katsura River and Togetsukyō — the classic Arashiyama lunch.

dish: Belgian- and American-style craft ales, ~10 taps incl. seasonals, at the brewery tasting room
w: Kyoto's flagship craft brewery, founded by an American, a Welshman and a Canadian; weekend tasting room at the brewery.

dish: Mugi-dai-mochi — fresh-pounded mochi with tsubu-an cooked over a wood-fired okudo-san
address: Opposite Katsura Imperial Villa, Nishikyō-ku, Kyoto
w: Long-established wagashi house facing Katsura Rikyū; red-bean paste still cooked the original way in a wood-fired okudo-san.

dish: Kitsune udon — thick udon hand-cut every morning, with Kyoto aburaage (kitsune ankake in winter)
address: Near Fushimi Inari Taisha, Fushimi-ku, Kyoto
w: The fox shrine's kitsune-udon stop: noodles made by hand each morning, tofu from a favourite Kyoto maker.

dish: Espresso and the 'Vermilion Plate' breakfast with Fushimi ham
address: Below Fushimi Inari Taisha, near JR Inari Stn, Fushimi-ku, Kyoto
w: Specialty-coffee stop at the foot of the torii tunnels — the pre-hike espresso.

dish: Shōjin-ryōri — Zen Buddhist vegetarian lunch courses in a temple-garden setting
address: Within the Daitoku-ji temple complex, Murasakino, Kita-ku, Kyoto
w: Shōjin lunches in a sub-temple garden of Daitoku-ji, served since 1963.

dish: Omen — dipping-style udon with kinpira burdock, sesame and seasonal vegetables
n: Omen Ginkakuji Honten (名代おめん 銀閣寺本店)
address: Below Ginkaku-ji (3 min from Ginkakuji-mae bus stop), Sakyō-ku, Kyoto
w: Since 1967 the Philosopher's-Path udon stop: thick noodles dipped in hot broth with a tray of condiments.

dish: Meidai mame-mochi — soft mochi studded with beans around sweet bean paste
w: Since 1899 the queue-worthy mame-mochi shop at the old Ōhara road entrance to the city.

dish: Warabi-mochi made with rare bracken-starch flour
n: Bunnosuke Chaya Kyoto Honten (京甘味 文の助茶屋 京都本店)
w: A sweet house founded in 1909; the classic warabi-mochi stop on the Kiyomizu approach.

dish: Yudofu set and soy-milk tofu manjū
n: Sōhonke Yudofu Okutan Kiyomizu (総本家ゆどうふ 奥丹清水)
w: The Kiyomizu branch of the centuries-old Okutan tofu house, in a garden off Ninenzaka.

dish: Coffee in a traditional Japanese townhouse on Ninenzaka
n: Starbucks Coffee Kyoto Ninenzaka Yasaka Chaya
w: The machiya Starbucks on the Kiyomizu approach — a traditional-house interior and a viral photo stop.

dish: Eight regional ramen styles from famous shops across Japan, under one roof
n: Kyoto Ramen Koji (京都拉麺小路)
w: Kyoto Station's ramen street — eight branches of famous regional shops on the 10th floor.
